newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia, UPM to sell chemicals jv.
newsitem.headline: Nokia, UPM to sell chemicals jv.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy and forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Friday they had agreed to sell their joint venture Finnish Chemicals to Finnish company Erikem Oy for 550 million markka.
Nokia and UPM-Kymmene each own 50 percent of Finnish Chemicals, which had a turnover of 829 million markka in 1995, the companies said in separate statements.
"Finnish Chemicals produces mainly bleaching chemicals for the wood processing industry," they said.
The joint-venture's Finnish Peroxide unit is not included in the deal. Finnish Peroxide, which produces hydrogen peroxide, is 50 percent-owned by Belgian Solvay S.A..
Both Nokia and UPM-Kymmene said they will retain their 25 percent stakes in Finnish Peroxide.
The major owners of Erikem include Finnish MB Equity Fund Ky and Tianguis Ltd, Prudental Venture Managers Ltd and HSBC Private Equite Europe Ltd of the United Kingdom.
